<summary>
  <request>Fix the pagination offset calculation in OrderQuery so the first page starts at zero.</request>
  <investigated>The pagination logic in OrderQuery.pageOffset and the corresponding OrderQueryTest#firstPageStartsAtZero behavior were examined.</investigated>
  <learned>OrderQuery.pageOffset now returns page * size without subtracting one, so page zero begins at offset zero.</learned>
  <completed>Updated OrderQuery.pageOffset to remove the extra -1 calculation, and OrderQueryTest#firstPageStartsAtZero passes.</completed>
  <next_steps>Continue with any requested pagination validation or regression testing for OrderQuery.</next_steps>
  <notes>The first-page offset bug was isolated to the extra subtraction in OrderQuery.pageOffset.</notes>
</summary>

<summary>
  <request>Fix the UserCache concurrency race so concurrent cache misses cannot both insert a null placeholder.</request>
  <investigated>The issue was examined in UserCache.get, where concurrent callers could both observe a missing entry and attempt to write a null placeholder. CacheConcurrencyTest was used to verify concurrent cache behavior.</investigated>
  <learned>UserCache.get now uses computeIfAbsent to load cache values atomically, preventing two concurrent callers from both writing a null placeholder. CacheConcurrencyTest passes with the updated UserCache.get behavior.</learned>
  <completed>UserCache.get was changed to load through computeIfAbsent, eliminating the concurrent null-placeholder write race. CacheConcurrencyTest passes after the change.</completed>
  <next_steps>Continue validating the UserCache concurrency fix with the existing test suite and address any remaining concurrency failures if they arise.</next_steps>
  <notes>The fix applies atomic cache loading at the UserCache.get call site rather than relying on separate null checks and writes.</notes>
</summary>

<summary>
  <request>Fix the race condition in UserCache and verify the change with CacheConcurrencyTest and the full verification suite.</request>
  <investigated>The implementation in src/main/java/com/acme/cache/UserCache.java was inspected, including UserCache.get and its previous direct cache lookup, along with CacheConcurrencyTest for concurrent access behavior.</investigated>
  <learned>UserCache.get now calls cache.computeIfAbsent(id, loader::load), allowing concurrent callers to share one cache-loading operation instead of both writing a null placeholder.</learned>
  <completed>UserCache.get was changed in src/main/java/com/acme/cache/UserCache.java to use computeIfAbsent, and CacheConcurrencyTest passes after the edit.</completed>
  <next_steps>Run the full verification suite to check for regressions beyond CacheConcurrencyTest.</next_steps>
  <notes>The race originated from UserCache.get using cache.get(id) before the load-and-store behavior was replaced with computeIfAbsent.</notes>
</summary>

<summary>
  <request>Fix the concurrency race in CounterService.increment and verify correct counting under parallel execution.</request>
  <investigated>CounterService.increment was examined for a race between reading and updating the counter. CounterServiceConcurrencyTest was used to validate concurrent increments with 1000 threads.</investigated>
  <learned>CounterService.increment now uses AtomicLong.incrementAndGet to perform an atomic counter update. CounterServiceConcurrencyTest produces a final count of 1000 when 1000 threads increment the counter concurrently.</learned>
  <completed>CounterService.increment was changed from a non-atomic get/set sequence to AtomicLong.incrementAndGet. CounterServiceConcurrencyTest passes with 1000 threads producing 1000.</completed>
  <next_steps>Continue reviewing or running relevant tests around CounterService and CounterServiceConcurrencyTest to check for regressions and broader concurrency issues.</next_steps>
  <notes>The original get/set pattern allowed concurrent increments to overwrite one another. AtomicLong.incrementAndGet removes that lost-update race.</notes>
</summary>

<summary>
  <request>Fix the race condition in CounterService by replacing the non-atomic counter update and verify it with concurrent execution.</request>
  <investigated>Inspected src/main/java/com/acme/metrics/CounterService.java and identified that CounterService.increment previously performed a counter.get() followed by counter.set(counter.get() + 1), which allowed concurrent updates to be lost.</investigated>
  <learned>CounterService.increment now uses AtomicLong.incrementAndGet for a single atomic update. CounterServiceConcurrencyTest exercises 1,000 threads and observes a final count of 1,000.</learned>
  <completed>CounterService.increment was changed from the get/set update sequence to return counter.incrementAndGet(), eliminating the race caused by concurrent get/set operations. CounterServiceConcurrencyTest passes with 1,000 threads producing 1,000.</completed>
  <next_steps>Run the full verification suite to check for regressions beyond CounterServiceConcurrencyTest.</next_steps>
  <notes>The fix targets concurrent increments in src/main/java/com/acme/metrics/CounterService.java and preserves the expected exact final count under heavy concurrency.</notes>
</summary>
